### No Whisper Ideas 🤫

###  

### Especially Earl

​Or, How to Market Now  
  
A big problem at Tacklebox HQ these days is what to do about cold outreach. AI has made cold outreach anywhere from 10 to 10,000 times more difficult (depending on your industry) for all the reasons we’ve talked about and don’t need to recap.So, what do you do?The answer is in a joke I heard from Malcolm Gladwell on the [How I Write Podcast](https://redacted.invalid/link-10). Gladwell originally heard it from comedian Demetri Martin, but I couldn’t find a clip of it anywhere so here’s Gladwell retelling it:_“My favorite joke, one I think about every single day, is by the comic Demetri Martin. It’s the greatest joke of all time. His setup involved thinking of phrases whose meaning was altered by adding the minimum number of words. He’s obsessed with language.__One of his best examples involves a restaurant bathroom sign that reads, “Employees must wash hands before returning to work.” He adds, “Especially Earl.” It’s one of the greatest literary jokes of all time. It’s brilliant because you immediately imagine Earl. In an instant, you know Earl, and suddenly the idea of staying in that restaurant becomes impossible. You have to leave.”_ Adding “especially Earl” is both hilarious and the new path for marketing. It’s how you stand out in an inbox that has 37 AI-generated cold emails and your hand-written one.Specificity works in a story because the more specific the detail the more trust it builds with the reader. A coffee shop on the corner of the street is forgettable, but a coffee shop on the corner of the street with two old men sitting in the window, waving their arms and arguing over a game of Guess Who is memorable. You’re interested. And you trust me to tell the rest of the story.Marketing copy is now entirely about specificity.The goal is to talk as specifically as you can about Momentum (what the customer is doing to try to solve the problem now) and a Quirk (their unique constraint that makes the common solutions to the problem useless). The more detail you can add to each, the more trust you’ll build. Note - none of this has anything to do with your _solution_ , which is secondary to the specifics of your customer’s problem.If you’re helping people find the right school to finish their college degree:_“You’re stuck at the application stage because no school will tell you if your decade-old credits count until after you’ve paid the app fee.”_ If you’re building loyalty programs for local coffee shops:_“You’ve been trying to set up a loyalty program for your coffee shop but you’ve only got one location and every solution is set up for franchises.”_ If you’re teaching healthcare companies how to responsibly use AI agents:_“You want your team using agents responsibly, but every AI safety course you’ve found ignores HIPAA.”_ The goal of an early-stage business is to know something about its customer that no one else does. This lets you solve the problem in peace - free from competitors and with an engaged customer group. This level of marketing specificity will help you attract those customers and also force you to focus on a tight subset with momentum and a quirk.Founders must lean into specifics to stand out. Especially Earl.
